top.title: Paul Finebaum calls out Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for ‘pandering’ after Ole Miss game move
top.description: Paul Finebaum went after Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny on SEC Network on Saturday morning, hours after Denny publicly objected to the SEC moving the Sooners’ game against the Ole Miss Rebels to Sunday. Speaking with Matt Barrie, Finebaum defended Commissioner Greg Sankey and then turned the conversation toward Denny’s first year in charge in Norman. Denny’s statement, posted around midnight, said Sankey moved the game over Oklahoma’s strong objection and warned that refusing to play at the new time would mean a forfeit. Dec 7, 2024; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN announcer Paul Finebaum before the 2024 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images “First of all, I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss, but I believe the administration at Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fan base at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know. But Mr. Sankey, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference, made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fan base, and what Roger Denny has been doing all year is pandering to his fan base. Before the season, Matt, he gave his football coach Brent Venables a contract extension. They were ranked number nine in the country. They have now lost four games and are out of the playoffs. Why did he do that? Because he’s an impulsive leader. He’s a former tax attorney. I’m not castigating tax attorneys or attorneys in general, but they run differently. And what he did here is really against the code of the SEC, to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fan base, who was already on tenterhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong. And quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum said. Paul Finebaum criticized Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for a midnight statement where he blasted the SEC’s decision to move the Ole Miss game to Sunday. https://t.co/MOmFA4SGk2 — Sports Fountain (@sportfountain) November 14, 2026 Denny announced Venables’ two-year extension on Aug. 20, two weeks before the opener, with Oklahoma ranked No. 9 in the preseason coaches poll and No. 10 by the AP. The new six-year contract runs through 2031 and is worth about $63 million. The Sooners take a 5-4 record into Sunday. Denny is a tax lawyer by training who spent nearly 15 years as a corporate attorney before moving into athletics administration at Illinois, and he took over at Oklahoma in February. When Paul Finebaum started questioning Roger Denny’s judgment Finebaum first tied Venables’ struggles to Denny in late September. After Oklahoma lost at Georgia, he went on The Matt Barrie Show and put the extension squarely on the athletic director.

top.title: Jaguars Arik Armstead fined for hip-drop tackle vs. Ravens in Week 9
top.description: Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images | Getty Images Arik Armstead will be fined $17,911 for a hip-drop tackle in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Baltimore Ravens. The fine for unnecessary roughness stems from a tackle on Derrick Henry on the Ravens’ very first offensive play of the third quarter. The play was a direct snap to Henry, who was stopped after just 1 yard by Armstead and Matt Dickerson. Armstead was not flagged for the play at the time. The fine is Armstead’s second of the season, after being fined 11,941 for a face mask penalty when the Jaguars played the Patriots back in Week 3 of the 2026 season. Armstead was the only Jaguars or Ravens player who was fined for their Week 9 play. Armstead, who signed with the Jaguars in 2024 after spending the first nine years of his career with the 49ers, has 14 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a pass breakup for the Jags this season. Armstead had two tackles in the Jaguars’ 33-10 victory, including the one he was fined for against the Joe Fagnano-led Ravens in Week 9. The funds the NFL collects through fines are donated to the NFLPA’s assistance to retired players, and the NFL Foundation and other nonprofit organizations that support kids’ sports leagues, community wellness initiatives, and the safety, health and well being of athletes at all levels of sports.

top.title: A player's 8-touchdown night fuels big upset in Bay Area HS football playoffs
top.description: A football sits on the sidelines before a high school game in Cumru, Pa., Oct. 9, 2020. (Ben Hasty/Reading Eagle/MediaNews Group via Getty Images) A massive high school football playoff upset in the Bay Area was punctuated by one of the most incredible individual performances in Northern California history. In the North Coast Section (NCS) Division 1 quarterfinals, No. 6 seed Acalanes pulled off the shocking win over No. 3 Pittsburg, winning 70-54 in a video game-like shootout. The game featured a ridiculous 1,200-plus yards of total offense and 18 touchdowns, but it's Dons quarterback Tyler Winkles' performance that will be the talk of the weekend. Winkles' final stat-line included 607 total yards - 471 passing yards and 136 rush yards -- and eight touchdowns. He also threw for two 2-point conversions. The 607 total yards is a North Coast Section record for most yards by a quarterback who also rushed for 100 yards in the same game, according to Cal-Hi Sports' Mark Tennis . Winkles, who is a senior, has no football scholarship offers and as a result, has committed to play baseball at Washington State, according to Bay Area News Group . "The baffling part is every college in the nation not offering him," Acalanes head coach Joel Isaac told Bay Area News Group. "I don't know what people are doing. Best athlete on the field every night." Winkles' record performance is all the more impressive when you take into account that he did it against a Pittsburg defense that features multiple D-I college prospects, notably edge rusher Terrance Murphy , who is committed to Fresno State, and safety Jeremiah Edwards , who's weighing offers from Cal, Oregon State, Washington State and Arizona. "All the other people are going to think it's an upset, but we knew," Winkles told Bay Area News Group after the game. "We were confident going into this game, I promise you that. This game made history for our school, but it's not over. We're still writing the chapters to our story." For Pittsburg, the loss ends the program's five-year reign as NCS Division I champions. It's also the Pirates' first playoff loss to a program not named De La Salle since 2016. Acalanes advances to the Division I semifinals for the second consecutive year, and will face No. 4-seeded San Ramon Valley next Friday. top.title: Michael Pittman Jr. says he feels healthy enough to return
top.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers made no trades ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, despite a clear need at wide receiver. Although the Steelers were interested in Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley and Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., a trade never materialized. While the receiver room has a bleak outlook right now, one of the Steelers’ highest paid receivers seems close to making his return from injured reserve. Steelers veteran wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has been out since Week 4 after suffering a plantar fasciitis injury. Still, it seems like his return could come sooner rather than later. “It feels good, and today was probably my best day yet,” Pittman told Brendan Howe of Steelers Now on Thursday. “Yesterday was good, today was even better, so definitely trending the right way.… I would love the opportunity to play this week, but that’s out of my control. I definitely let them know today that I thought it was good.” Pittman Jr. remains on injured reserve, with the Steelers yet to open his 21-day practice window. The receiver was seen working off to the side this week and even ran during warmups. Although Pittman Jr. will be out this week against Cincinnati, the receiver feels healthy enough to go. The Steelers acquired Pittman Jr. in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts this past March. top.title: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable?
top.description: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable? Aston Villa have told suitors that Boubacar Kamara is not for sale in January or beyond, according to Football Insider. Former Villa scout Mick Brown says Unai Emery treats the 26-year-old France international as a guaranteed starter and has no intention of weakening a midfield that is already short of options. Chelsea , Inter Milan and Saudi Pro League clubs have all been linked with him, yet Brown insists none of them will get a hearing. Why Villa have no choice Amadou Onana tore his cruciate ligament in July, and FotMob lists mid-April 2027 as his expected return, so the player best suited to work alongside Kamara will miss almost the whole season. Brown also claims Villa are trying to extend Ross Barkley’s stay. The 32-year-old has a long record of fitness setbacks, so he works as cover rather than a replacement. What Kamara gives Emery Kamara rarely makes highlight reels, but he keeps Villa’s shape together. FotMob credits him with 28 tackles, 56% of his duels won and 86.3% pass accuracy across 883 Premier League minutes this season. He can also drop into central defence, which Emery has needed before. The weaknesses are just as clear. He hasn’t scored, has managed only 0.14 expected goals from three shots and offers little in the final third. His body has let him down too, with a cruciate injury in February 2024 and a hamstring problem at the start of last season. Should Aston Villa treat Kamara as untouchable? MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 08: Boubacar Kamara of Aston Villa reacts after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Yes, and the reasoning is about this season rather than sentiment. Villa conceded three against Barcelona and four at Manchester United in their last two games. A team leaking goals like that cannot sell the one midfielder who protects their back line, least of all when Onana is out, and no January signing at Kamara’s level is likely to be affordable. His contract runs to 2030, so Villa face no pressure to cash in. If a huge bid arrives next summer, with Onana back and fit, the conversation changes. The real worry is cover. Kamara contributes almost nothing going forward, so Emery needs John McGinn, now 32, to provide the creativity next to him. Villa should use January to add one more holding midfielder, even on loan, rather than rely on Barkley’s body staying intact.

top.title: Real Madrid sees Arsenal man as the profile they need to sign in January
top.description: Real Madrid sees Arsenal man as the profile they need to sign in January Martin Zubimendi remains firmly on Real Madrid’s radar as the Spanish giants consider trying to sign him from Arsenal in one of the upcoming transfer windows. Madrid have followed the midfielder since his time at Real Sociedad, but Arsenal won the race for his signature after the Spanish club decided against acting on a recommendation from their manager at the time, Xabi Alonso. Alonso now manages Chelsea and is also interested in bringing Zubimendi to the Premier League club . However, the midfielder could favour a return to Spain with Real Madrid rather than making another move within English football. Although Zubimendi is no longer a regular starter at Arsenal, the Gunners still regard him as one of their most important players. They want to keep him beyond this season and are unlikely to welcome interest from other clubs. Real Madrid identify Zubimendi as midfield target Madrid are aware of Arsenal’s position, but that has not stopped them from considering a move. According to Fichajes , the club have identified Zubimendi as the player who could address their midfield problems and provide the missing link between their defence and attack. The Spanish giants believe his qualities could improve their options in the middle of the pitch. Despite their recent performances under Jose Mourinho, they remain interested in adding another midfielder to their squad, with Zubimendi reportedly at the top of their list. His experience in Spanish football and understanding of the demands of the game in La Liga could make him an attractive option for Madrid as they assess their recruitment plans. (Photo by Jack Thomas/Getty Images) January approach remains possible Real Madrid would ideally prefer to wait until the end of the season before making a move for the Arsenal midfielder. However, there is a possibility that they could approach the Gunners in January. Zubimendi’s limited playing time at Arsenal could encourage Madrid to test the club’s resolve sooner rather than later. They may believe the situation gives them an opportunity to convince him to consider a return to Spain. Arsenal, however, still value the midfielder highly and want him to remain part of their plans. top.title: Comeback kid Joseph thrills as England eye All Blacks
top.description: Eddie Jones aired a complaint about Twickenham's in-stadium experience when he appeared on BBC Radio 5 Live this week. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. With junior tickets on sale at £15, there was a different atmosphere from usual. The decibels were higher, the demographic was younger, the spirits a little lighter. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. He struggled for game time and fitness at Harlequins after London Irish's bankruptcy forced him to move on from his boyhood club. An auto-immune condition that cost him the hearing in his left ear was one setback at the Stoop. But, as part of a rat pack of exciting young English-qualified backs at Gloucester this season, he has been superb: a swerving, offloading, game-breaking threat either on the wing or in midfield. England deployed him out wide, to bring some of the razzle-dazzle that they lost as Immanuel Feyi-Waboso limped out of their autumn campaign. Reports from Pennyhill Park during the week had suggested Joseph was doing a fine job of replicating Feyi-Waboso's explosive elusiveness. He certainly did on Twickenham's main stage, finishing chances with the same pace and power. "He is pretty similar to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the way he plays his game," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live. "He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people." Joseph's cartwheeling plant of the ball over the line for his fourth summed up his exuberance. In the aftermath of that score, Japan flanker Ben Gunter put a consoling arm around full-back Kazuma Ueda, who had been comprehensively burned in a race to the corner. Japan couldn't get near Joseph, whose first try came after just 60 seconds and his hat-trick score in the 19th minute. top.title: Valley Central football got into the Section 9 Class AA final by forfeit. Then, the Vikings won it.
top.description: The Valley Central football team beat Newburgh Free Academy for the Section 9 Class AA title on Saturday. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The Valley Central football team, which was inserted into the Section 9 Class AA championship game after previously undefeated Middletown was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory against it due to the use of an ineligible player, won the sectional final Saturday afternoon in a stunning upset. Valley Central, which entered Saturday's Class AA final against Newburgh Free Academy at Monroe-Woodbury High School with a 5-5 record, came away with a shocking 16-6 win to earn a berth in the state tournament. The Vikings were originally eliminated from the Section 9 playoffs last weekend with a 48-15 loss to Middletown. But, in the days following the game, it emerged that Middletown had used an ineligible player - a soccer player who was used as a kickoff specialist - in that semifinal win and would be forced to forfeit. The decision led to a hasty appeals process and an eventual petition for emergency relief in state Supreme Court that was withdrawn Friday. State rules require an athlete to be an eligible participant for a minimum of three regular-season football games in order to be eligible for postseason play. The player, according to court documents, only played in one regular-season game and was on the sideline for another before he participated in the semifinal game. The Middletown school district appealed to both Section 9 and the New York State Public High School Athletic Association to overturn the decision, but was rejected on both occasions. The district then went to court seeking to have the team's place in the sectional final restored, but the petition was withdrawn following a Friday afternoon hearing. Valley Central will play the winner of Saturday's Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl between Saratoga Springs and Christian Brothers Academy in a state quarterfinal on Nov. 21 at Colonie High School. Elsewhere in the state, a similar situation has affected the Section 4 Class D championship game. Delaware Academy, the No. 2-ranked Class D team in the state, was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory over Deposit/Hancock due to the same rule that led to Middletown's forfeit. Delaware Academy also appealed to its section and NYSPHSAA, which was ultimately unsuccessful. Deposit/Hancock will face Tioga for the Section 4 Class D title on Sunday. nigeria.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
nigeria.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway. The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. nigeria.description: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”. He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”. It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”. But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. nigeria.description: The vice presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has described the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as incorruptible. Kwankwaso made the declaration on Saturday at the 5th convocation ceremony of the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. Kwankwaso said the attribute is key and needed in governance of the nation. “One thing I noted in the last few months that we have been working together is that Peter Obi is incorruptible. He’s not somebody that you can go and start thinking of corruption around him, and that is very key in governance in this country,” he said. Kwankwaso pledged that an NDC-led administration would prioritise free education to ensure that no child was denied access to schooling due to financial constraints. “We have so much in common, especially in the issue of education. We believe that together it will be extremely difficult to see how any child will go around in this part of the country or elsewhere begging for what to eat. “In other words, we are working towards free education to ensure that our children are not denied going to school because the parents cannot afford to pay school fees or other expenses. In his remarks, Obi pledged to revive moribund industries in Kano to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities. He described Kano as central to Nigeria’s economic development, saying efforts to rebuild the country’s economy must begin with the state. “If we want to fix the North and Nigeria, we must start from Kano. This town represents the soul of Nigeria,” he said. Obi urged the graduates to embrace entrepreneurship, noting that small businesses play a critical role in employment generation and economic growth. nigeria.title: Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Portugal have announced a redesign of the No. 7 on their national team shirts in tribute to former captain Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced the change on Saturday, saying the new design would preserve the legacy of the number associated with the 41-year-old forward. In a statement shared by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, the federation said the decision was another way to immortalise the significance of the number and honour Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese football. “This is another way to eternalise the meaning of such a special number and honour the legacy it represents for us. “Because there are stories, memories, all the achievements and emotions, which will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the sweater, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalisation of the story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the statement read. Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on November 5, bringing an end to his 23-year international career. In a message to Portuguese supporters, the forward said it was time to hand back the national team shirt and captain’s armband after enjoying the privilege of representing his country for more than two decades. “For 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world,” he said. Ronaldo finished his international career as Portugal’s record appearance-maker, with 234 caps, and all-time leading scorer, with 146 goals. He also captained the country to its first European Championship title in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. entertainment.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. entertainment.description: Africa’s economic story is increasingly being written by women. Across the continent, women own and operate a remarkable share of small and growing enterprises, sustain household and community economies, and drive innovation in sectors from finance and technology to the creative industries. Yet the gap between participation and power remains wide. Too many women-led businesses stay small, under-capitalised and absent from the rooms where markets, policy and capital are shaped. On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the HerSphere Global Summit 2026 will gather a distinguished assembly of leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre, Lagos, Nigeria, to confront that gap directly. Proceedings begin promptly at 9:00 a.m. A Theme That Demands Action This year’s theme, “ Her Enterprise, Africa Advantage: Moving Women-Led Businesses Beyond Participation to Economic Power,” reflects a deliberate shift in the conversation. The question is no longer whether women belong in Africa’s economy — that has long been settled. The question is how women-led enterprises can scale, command capital, influence policy and build institutions that endure. The summit is designed to move beyond inspiration to strategy: how women founders access growth finance, how they enter regional and global value chains, how public institutions and private capital can work together to back them, and how today’s enterprises become tomorrow’s market leaders. An Exceptional Line-Up of Voices HerSphere Global Summit 2026 brings together an exceptional roster of women who have shaped Nigeria’s and Africa’s judicial, public, financial, entrepreneurial and creative landscapes: • Hon. Backed by Institutions That Shape the Economy The summit is supported by a strong coalition of partners: the Lagos State Government, the Office of Sustainable Development Goals (Lagos Global), the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), Delphino Entertainment, and SheMeansBusiness by BusinessDay. Their involvement underscores a growing recognition across government, capital markets and media that empowering women-led enterprise is not a social side-project — it is core economic strategy. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike , raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara . entertainment.title: FWIFT 2026 Convention Communique: Industry Leaders Charge Women in Media to Embrace Cross-Border Growth
entertainment.description: The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency. Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) , the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago , interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed , filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede. Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions: “Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.” Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.” FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media. For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media. About FWIFT Nigeria The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. sports.title: Paul Finebaum calls out Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for ‘pandering’ after Ole Miss game move
sports.description: Paul Finebaum went after Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny on SEC Network on Saturday morning, hours after Denny publicly objected to the SEC moving the Sooners’ game against the Ole Miss Rebels to Sunday. Speaking with Matt Barrie, Finebaum defended Commissioner Greg Sankey and then turned the conversation toward Denny’s first year in charge in Norman. Denny’s statement, posted around midnight, said Sankey moved the game over Oklahoma’s strong objection and warned that refusing to play at the new time would mean a forfeit. Dec 7, 2024; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN announcer Paul Finebaum before the 2024 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images “First of all, I understand the frustration, and none of us really know what happened to Ole Miss, but I believe the administration at Ole Miss did everything they could. What I don’t think is correct is Roger Denny, the athletic director there, pathetically pandering to his fan base at midnight to try to cover up whatever, I don’t know. But Mr. Sankey, the commissioner of the Southeastern Conference, made a decision for the entire conference and for the safety of everyone. He’s not concerned about what you’re doing with your fan base, and what Roger Denny has been doing all year is pandering to his fan base. Before the season, Matt, he gave his football coach Brent Venables a contract extension. They were ranked number nine in the country. They have now lost four games and are out of the playoffs. Why did he do that? Because he’s an impulsive leader. He’s a former tax attorney. I’m not castigating tax attorneys or attorneys in general, but they run differently. And what he did here is really against the code of the SEC, to call out a commissioner during a national crisis and emergency. He’s thinking about himself and his fan base, who was already on tenterhooks because of the season, and I think he is dead wrong. And quite frankly, I think it’s unbecoming of a leader in college athletics or anywhere to do what he did,” Finebaum said. Paul Finebaum criticized Oklahoma AD Roger Denny for a midnight statement where he blasted the SEC’s decision to move the Ole Miss game to Sunday. https://t.co/MOmFA4SGk2 — Sports Fountain (@sportfountain) November 14, 2026 Denny announced Venables’ two-year extension on Aug. 20, two weeks before the opener, with Oklahoma ranked No. 9 in the preseason coaches poll and No. 10 by the AP. The new six-year contract runs through 2031 and is worth about $63 million. The Sooners take a 5-4 record into Sunday. Denny is a tax lawyer by training who spent nearly 15 years as a corporate attorney before moving into athletics administration at Illinois, and he took over at Oklahoma in February. When Paul Finebaum started questioning Roger Denny’s judgment Finebaum first tied Venables’ struggles to Denny in late September. sports.title: A player's 8-touchdown night fuels big upset in Bay Area HS football playoffs
sports.description: A football sits on the sidelines before a high school game in Cumru, Pa., Oct. 9, 2020. (Ben Hasty/Reading Eagle/MediaNews Group via Getty Images) A massive high school football playoff upset in the Bay Area was punctuated by one of the most incredible individual performances in Northern California history. In the North Coast Section (NCS) Division 1 quarterfinals, No. 6 seed Acalanes pulled off the shocking win over No. 3 Pittsburg, winning 70-54 in a video game-like shootout. The game featured a ridiculous 1,200-plus yards of total offense and 18 touchdowns, but it's Dons quarterback Tyler Winkles' performance that will be the talk of the weekend. Winkles' final stat-line included 607 total yards - 471 passing yards and 136 rush yards -- and eight touchdowns. He also threw for two 2-point conversions. The 607 total yards is a North Coast Section record for most yards by a quarterback who also rushed for 100 yards in the same game, according to Cal-Hi Sports' Mark Tennis . Winkles, who is a senior, has no football scholarship offers and as a result, has committed to play baseball at Washington State, according to Bay Area News Group . "The baffling part is every college in the nation not offering him," Acalanes head coach Joel Isaac told Bay Area News Group. "I don't know what people are doing. Best athlete on the field every night." Winkles' record performance is all the more impressive when you take into account that he did it against a Pittsburg defense that features multiple D-I college prospects, notably edge rusher Terrance Murphy , who is committed to Fresno State, and safety Jeremiah Edwards , who's weighing offers from Cal, Oregon State, Washington State and Arizona. "All the other people are going to think it's an upset, but we knew," Winkles told Bay Area News Group after the game. "We were confident going into this game, I promise you that. This game made history for our school, but it's not over. We're still writing the chapters to our story." For Pittsburg, the loss ends the program's five-year reign as NCS Division I champions. It's also the Pirates' first playoff loss to a program not named De La Salle since 2016. Acalanes advances to the Division I semifinals for the second consecutive year, and will face No. 4-seeded San Ramon Valley next Friday. sports.title: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable?
sports.description: Aston Villa Block Chelsea And Inter Raid On French Star: Is He Untouchable? Aston Villa have told suitors that Boubacar Kamara is not for sale in January or beyond, according to Football Insider. Former Villa scout Mick Brown says Unai Emery treats the 26-year-old France international as a guaranteed starter and has no intention of weakening a midfield that is already short of options. Chelsea , Inter Milan and Saudi Pro League clubs have all been linked with him, yet Brown insists none of them will get a hearing. Why Villa have no choice Amadou Onana tore his cruciate ligament in July, and FotMob lists mid-April 2027 as his expected return, so the player best suited to work alongside Kamara will miss almost the whole season. Brown also claims Villa are trying to extend Ross Barkley’s stay. The 32-year-old has a long record of fitness setbacks, so he works as cover rather than a replacement. What Kamara gives Emery Kamara rarely makes highlight reels, but he keeps Villa’s shape together. FotMob credits him with 28 tackles, 56% of his duels won and 86.3% pass accuracy across 883 Premier League minutes this season. He can also drop into central defence, which Emery has needed before. The weaknesses are just as clear. He hasn’t scored, has managed only 0.14 expected goals from three shots and offers little in the final third. His body has let him down too, with a cruciate injury in February 2024 and a hamstring problem at the start of last season. Should Aston Villa treat Kamara as untouchable? MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 08: Boubacar Kamara of Aston Villa reacts after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Yes, and the reasoning is about this season rather than sentiment. Villa conceded three against Barcelona and four at Manchester United in their last two games. A team leaking goals like that cannot sell the one midfielder who protects their back line, least of all when Onana is out, and no January signing at Kamara’s level is likely to be affordable. His contract runs to 2030, so Villa face no pressure to cash in. If a huge bid arrives next summer, with Onana back and fit, the conversation changes. The real worry is cover. Kamara contributes almost nothing going forward, so Emery needs John McGinn, now 32, to provide the creativity next to him. Villa should use January to add one more holding midfielder, even on loan, rather than rely on Barkley’s body staying intact.

"Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. He struggled for game time and fitness at Harlequins after London Irish's bankruptcy forced him to move on from his boyhood club. An auto-immune condition that cost him the hearing in his left ear was one setback at the Stoop. Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3. sports.title: Valley Central football got into the Section 9 Class AA final by forfeit. Then, the Vikings won it.
sports.description: The Valley Central football team beat Newburgh Free Academy for the Section 9 Class AA title on Saturday. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The Valley Central football team, which was inserted into the Section 9 Class AA championship game after previously undefeated Middletown was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory against it due to the use of an ineligible player, won the sectional final Saturday afternoon in a stunning upset. Valley Central, which entered Saturday's Class AA final against Newburgh Free Academy at Monroe-Woodbury High School with a 5-5 record, came away with a shocking 16-6 win to earn a berth in the state tournament. The Vikings were originally eliminated from the Section 9 playoffs last weekend with a 48-15 loss to Middletown. But, in the days following the game, it emerged that Middletown had used an ineligible player - a soccer player who was used as a kickoff specialist - in that semifinal win and would be forced to forfeit. The decision led to a hasty appeals process and an eventual petition for emergency relief in state Supreme Court that was withdrawn Friday. State rules require an athlete to be an eligible participant for a minimum of three regular-season football games in order to be eligible for postseason play. The player, according to court documents, only played in one regular-season game and was on the sideline for another before he participated in the semifinal game. The Middletown school district appealed to both Section 9 and the New York State Public High School Athletic Association to overturn the decision, but was rejected on both occasions. The district then went to court seeking to have the team's place in the sectional final restored, but the petition was withdrawn following a Friday afternoon hearing. Valley Central will play the winner of Saturday's Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl between Saratoga Springs and Christian Brothers Academy in a state quarterfinal on Nov. 21 at Colonie High School. Elsewhere in the state, a similar situation has affected the Section 4 Class D championship game. Delaware Academy, the No. 2-ranked Class D team in the state, was forced to forfeit its semifinal victory over Deposit/Hancock due to the same rule that led to Middletown's forfeit. Delaware Academy also appealed to its section and NYSPHSAA, which was ultimately unsuccessful. Deposit/Hancock will face Tioga for the Section 4 Class D title on Sunday. sports.title: Cam Collier, Carlos Sanchez lead Reds prospects in need of Rule 5 protection
sports.description: KNOXVILLE, TN - SEPTEMBER 03: Cam Collier #6 of the Chattanooga Lookouts celebrates in the dugout during the game between the Chattanooga Lookouts and the Knoxville Smokies at Covenant Health Park on Thursday, September 3, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Ryan Beatty/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) Tuesday, November 17th at 6:00 PM ET marks the deadline for all 30 MLB clubs to add players to their respective 40-man rosters in order to keep them protected from selection in December’s Rule 5 Draft. Said draft, you’ll recall, is a way of preventing teams from hoarding their best and brightest prospects in the minor leagues while blocking their paths for promotion, a field-leveling administrative mechanism that at least gives a little bet of help balancing the power of the 30 individual franchises. As MLB Pipeline noted, there are four current minor leaguers who have been in the franchise long enough to be eligible for Rule 5 selection that also find themselves ranked among the Top 30 within the Cincinnati Reds system. That list is headlined by former 1st round pick Cam Collier as well as Carlos Sanchez, who excelled during the 2026 regular season before bursting even further onto the scene by slashing .300/.425/.571 (.997 OPS) in 20 games in Arizona Fall League play. 1B Carter Graham, who knocked the stitches out of baseballs throughout his own breakout 2026 season, also joins them, as does fellow former 1st round pick Jay Allen II. There are two important caveats worth noting regarding the Rule 5 Draft. Any team that selects a player must keep said player on their active roster for the entire season lest they be forced to offer them back to their original franchise; that means that even though an eligible player may well be uber-talented, they aren’t necessarily going to get picked if they aren’t actually ready for big league play just yet. The other caveat is 2026 specific, as the Rule 5 Draft is scheduled for December 9th during the Winter Meetings…but that’s after the expiration of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement is set to expire on December 1st. It remains to be seen just how much that will impact all the usual administrative deadlines and procedures we see during typical MLB offseasons, and there’s a chance the draft itself gets kicked much further down the road altogether. As for the Reds in particular, they have 37 players currently on their 40-man roster after adding back players who finished the regular season on the 60-day IL. So, if they’re to actually protect all four of the players listed above (and/or anyone else that’s eligible and not one of MLB Pipeline’s Top 30 prospects in the system) they’re going to have to remove someone who’s currently holding a spot. We’ll find out more come Tuesday!

science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.
